title: Declaration in Support of Application for Immigrant Visa
text:
UNITED STATES DEPARTMENT OF HOMELAND SECURITY
U.S. CITIZENSHIP AND IMMIGRATION SERVICES

In the Matter of: 
Petitioner: Maria Elena Vasquez née Ramirez, also formerly known as Maria Elena Ramirez de la Cruz
Beneficiary: Andrés Felipe Herrera

I, Maria Elena Vasquez, pursuant to 8 U.S.C. § 1154, do hereby declare and state under penalty of perjury as follows:

1. I am a naturalized citizen of the United States, born on March 14, 1971, in Guadalajara, Jalisco, Mexico. My current residential address is 4527 Elmwood Lane, Houston, Harris County, Texas 77004. My telephone number is (713) 555-0182. My email address is maria.vasquez@inventedmail.net.

2. I have been lawfully admitted to the United States and have maintained status as a lawful permanent resident since 2001. I was naturalized as a U.S. citizen on June 15, 2010, in Houston, Texas.

3. I am petitioning for my husband, Andrés Felipe Herrera, a citizen of Colombia, born on November 22, 1975. We were married on October 12, 2019, in Houston, Texas. Our marriage is bona fide and not entered into for the purpose of evading immigration laws.

4. I have never been married to any other person, except for a prior marriage that ended in divorce on March 3, 2005. My maiden name is Ramirez, and I was formerly known as Maria Elena Ramirez de la Cruz during that prior marriage, but I have since resumed my maiden name and later adopted my current married name upon my marriage to Andrés.

5. My husband and I reside together at the above address. We share financial responsibilities, including a joint bank account at First National Bank of Texas, account number ending in 4567. We also have a joint lease agreement for our apartment at the address above.

6. I am employed as a senior project manager at Apex Construction Solutions, LLC, located at 9000 Commerce Park Drive, Houston, Texas 77036. My employer has provided a letter confirming my employment and salary. I have also filed joint federal income tax returns with my husband for the years 2020, 2021, and 2022.

7. I submit the following evidence in support of this petition: (a) copies of our marriage certificate, (b) birth certificates of our minor children, (c) photographs of our family gatherings, (d) affidavits from friends and family, and (e) financial records showing commingling of assets.

8. I am aware that making false statements on this declaration is subject to penalties under 18 U.S.C. § 1546. I declare that the foregoing is true and correct.

Executed on January 12, 2024, at Houston, Texas.

Maria Elena Vasquez
(Maria Elena Vasquez née Ramirez, formerly Maria Elena Ramirez de la Cruz)

Subscribed and sworn to before me this 12th day of January, 2024.

Notary Public, State of Texas
My Commission Expires: December 31, 2026

This declaration is submitted in connection with the case of Vasquez v. Herrera, No. 2024-IM-0187 (Houston Immigration Court). See also Matter of Cruz, 25 I&N Dec. 410 (BIA 2019).

title: Affidavit of Financial Support and Intent to Petition for Alien Relative
text:
UNITED STATES DISTRICT COURT FOR THE SOUTHERN DISTRICT OF TEXAS
HOUSTON DIVISION

Civil Action No. H-24-0187

IN RE: APPLICATION FOR ADMISSION OF NONIMMIGRANT WORKER

AFFIDAVIT OF SUPPORT

I, Jennifer Lynn Whitfield, formerly known as Jennifer Lynn Turner, currently residing at 2210 Marigold Street, Houston, Harris County, Texas 77005, do hereby swear and affirm as follows:

1. I am the petitioner in this matter. My Social Security Number is 456-78-9123. My date of birth is March 14, 1971, and I am a citizen of the United States.

2. I am the sister of the beneficiary, David Alan Whitfield, a citizen of the United Kingdom, born on June 3, 1980. I am petitioning for David to obtain an immigrant visa as a sibling of a U.S. citizen.

3. I am employed as a staff attorney at the law firm of Martínez & Associates, P.C., with offices at 500 Travis Street, Suite 1200, Houston, Texas 77002. My annual income for the past three years has been $85,000, $92,000, and $95,000, respectively. I am filing this affidavit to demonstrate that I can support David at 125% above the federal poverty guidelines.

4. I am married to Robert James Whitfield, and we have two minor children. We have a joint savings account at Texas Coastal Bank, account number 987-654-3210. I also have a brokerage account with Vanguard Investments, account number 555-123-4567.

5. I have never been convicted of a felony or a crime involving moral turpitude. I have not received any public assistance, except for unemployment benefits during the COVID-19 pandemic, which are not considered in the public charge determination.

6. I understand that this affidavit is a contract between me and the U.S. government. I agree to provide support to David until he becomes a U.S. citizen or has worked 40 quarters of coverage under the Social Security Act.

7. I have attached copies of my tax returns, W-2 forms, and bank statements. I have also submitted letters from my employer confirming my employment and salary.

8. I am willing to undergo a background check and provide any additional information requested by the immigration authorities.

I declare under penalty of perjury that the foregoing is true and correct.

Executed on February 15, 2024, at Houston, Texas.

Jennifer Lynn Whitfield
(Jennifer Lynn Whitfield, formerly known as Jennifer Lynn Turner)

Subscribed and sworn to before me on February 15, 2024.

Notary Public, State of Texas
My Commission Expires: January 31, 2027

This affidavit is submitted in connection with the matter of Whitfield v. Johnson, No. H-24-0187 (S.D. Tex. 2024). See also United States v. Cuevas, 512 F.3d 162 (5th Cir. 2008).

title: Motion for Continuance in Removal Proceedings
text:
UNITED STATES DEPARTMENT OF JUSTICE
EXECUTIVE OFFICE FOR IMMIGRATION REVIEW
IMMIGRATION COURT, HOUSTON, TEXAS

In the Matter of: 
Respondent: Carlos Eduardo Mendoza
File No.: A-098-765-432

MOTION FOR CONTINUANCE

COMES NOW the Respondent, Carlos Eduardo Mendoza, by and through his attorney, Sarah Michelle Nguyen of Nguyen & Patel, LLP, and respectfully moves this Court to continue the removal hearing scheduled for March 10, 2024.

I. INTRODUCTION

1. Respondent is a native and citizen of Honduras, born on April 12, 1985. He is currently in removal proceedings. Respondent requests a continuance to allow his counsel to prepare and file an application for asylum, withholding of removal, and protection under the Convention Against Torture.

2. This motion is supported by the attached declaration of Respondent and the declaration of his wife, Juana Maria Torres Mendoza.

II. FACTUAL BACKGROUND

3. Respondent entered the United States on or about July 15, 2022, without inspection. He was placed in removal proceedings on August 3, 2022, and has been detained at the Houston Processing Center since that time.

4. Respondent fears persecution in Honduras due to his membership in a particular social group, namely individuals who have opposed gang violence. He has received threats from MS-13 and other criminal organizations.

5. Respondent's wife is a lawful permanent resident. They have three minor children, all born in the United States. Respondent's wife resides at 1034 Cedar Bend Drive, Houston, Texas 77003. Her phone number is (713) 555-0174, and her email is juana.torres@invented.net.

III. LEGAL ARGUMENT

6. Under 8 C.F.R. § 1003.29, an Immigration Judge may grant a motion for continuance for good cause shown. The Board of Immigration Appeals has held that a party requesting a continuance must demonstrate that the request is not for purposes of delay and that specific evidence exists to support the application. See Matter of Linde, 21 I&N Dec. 442 (BIA 1996).

7. Respondent has been unable to obtain necessary legal representation until recently. His prior attorney, Thomas J. Bradley, withdrew from representation due to a conflict of interest. The current counsel has not had sufficient time to review the case file and prepare the necessary applications.

8. Respondent has been diligent in pursuing his case. He filed a pro se motion for a change of venue, which was denied. He has also requested a bond hearing, which is scheduled for April 5, 2024.

IV. CONCLUSION

9. For the foregoing reasons, Respondent respectfully requests that the Court grant a continuance of at least 60 days to allow counsel to prepare and file the necessary applications.

Dated: February 28, 2024

Respectfully submitted,

Sarah Michelle Nguyen
Nguyen & Patel, LLP
Attorney for Respondent

Certificate of Service: I certify that a copy of this motion was served on the U.S. Attorney's Office, Southern District of Texas, and the Department of Homeland Security counsel on February 28, 2024.

This motion is filed in the matter of Mendoza v. Garland, No. A-098-765-432 (Immigration Court 2024). See also Velasquez v. Holder, 512 F.3d 162 (5th Cir. 2008).

title: Application for Asylum and Withholding of Removal
text:
UNITED STATES DEPARTMENT OF HOMELAND SECURITY
U.S. CITIZENSHIP AND IMMIGRATION SERVICES

Form I-589, Application for Asylum and for Withholding of Removal

Applicant: Fatima Zahra Al-Hassan, formerly known as Fatima Zahra Okafor (maiden name: Okafor)

I, Fatima Zahra Al-Hassan, hereby submit this application for asylum and withholding of removal. My date of birth is March 14, 1971. I am a native and citizen of Nigeria. My current address is 2310 Palm Grove Circle, Houston, Texas 77030. My phone number is (713) 555-0119. My email address is fatima.alhassan@inventedmail.com.

STATEMENT OF FACTS:

I was born in Lagos, Nigeria. I am married to Ibrahim Al-Hassan, a Nigerian national. I have two children. I am a member of the Igbo ethnic group and practice Christianity. I fear persecution from Boko Haram and other Islamic extremist groups in Nigeria.

On April 15, 2022, armed men attacked my village. They killed my father and burned our home. I fled to the United States on May 2, 2022, on a B-2 visa. I have remained in the United States beyond my authorized stay.

I am applying for asylum because I have a well-founded fear of persecution on account of my religion and ethnicity. I am also applying for withholding of removal under 8 U.S.C. § 1231(b)(3).

During my time in the United States, I have been residing with my cousin, Amina Okafor. I have also received support from the Nigerian American Community Center, a non-profit organization located at 4500 Main Street, Houston, Texas 77002.

I have not been convicted of any crime. I have not been involved in any terrorist activities. I am not subject to any bars to asylum.

I understand that providing false information on this application may result in criminal prosecution under 18 U.S.C. § 1546.

I request that my application be considered by an asylum officer. I also request a hearing before an immigration judge if my application is not approved.

I declare under penalty of perjury that the foregoing is true and correct.

Executed on March 1, 2024, at Houston, Texas.

Fatima Zahra Al-Hassan

This application is filed in connection with the matter of Al-Hassan v. Garland, No. 2024-AS-0157 (Immigration Court 2024). See also I.N.S. v. Elias-Zacarias, 512 F.3d 162 (5th Cir. 2008).

title: Bond Hearing Brief for Respondent in Removal Proceedings
text:
UNITED STATES DEPARTMENT OF JUSTICE
EXECUTIVE OFFICE FOR IMMIGRATION REVIEW
IMMIGRATION COURT, HOUSTON, TEXAS

In re: Respondent: Diego Alejandro Fuentes
File No.: A-045-987-654

BRIEF IN SUPPORT OF RELEASE ON BOND

COMES NOW Respondent, Diego Alejandro Fuentes, by and through his attorney, Paul Richard Gonzalez of Gonzalez & Rivera, P.C., and submits this brief in support of his release on bond.

I. INTRODUCTION

Respondent is a native and citizen of Peru, born on May 23, 1988. He was placed in removal proceedings on January 10, 2024, after being arrested by U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE). Respondent is currently detained at the Houston Detention Facility. He requests a bond in the amount of $5,000.

II. FACTUAL BACKGROUND

Respondent has resided in the United States since 2015. He is married to a U.S. citizen, Emily Ann Fuentes (née Thompson). They have two minor children. Respondent is the sole breadwinner for his family. His wife and children reside at 4507 Gardenia Avenue, Houston, Texas 77004.

Respondent has no criminal history. He has no prior immigration violations. He has strong ties to the community, including a job as a construction foreman at Texas Builders Corp. d/b/a Texas Home Improvements, located at 1200 Industrial Parkway, Houston, Texas 77008.

III. LEGAL ARGUMENT

An immigration judge may set a bond pursuant to 8 U.S.C. § 1226(a). The respondent must demonstrate that he is not a danger to the community and that he poses no flight risk. The Board of Immigration Appeals has outlined factors in Matter of Guerra, 24 I&N Dec. 37 (BIA 2006).

Respondent qualifies for release. He has no criminal record, is a long-time resident with family ties, and has a stable employment history. His wife can post the bond, and they have a substantial equity in their home, which serves as an assurance of appearance.

IV. CONCLUSION

For these reasons, Respondent requests that the Court set a reasonable bond and release him from custody.

Dated: March 5, 2024

Respectfully submitted,

Paul Richard Gonzalez
Gonzalez & Rivera, P.C.

Certificate of Service: I served this brief on the Department of Homeland Security counsel and the U.S. Attorney's Office on March 5, 2024.

This brief is submitted in the matter of Fuentes v. Johnson, No. A-045-987-654 (Immigration Court 2024). See also Matter of Ramirez, 25 I&N Dec. 410 (BIA 2019).
